description.narrative: More than 95% of the worldwide saffron production comes from Iran. Saffron production capacity in Iran has increased from 152 tonnes in 2000 to 250 tonnes in 2009, +68%. The export value during the same period has increased from US $51 Mil to US $255 Mil, +400%. The share of Iranian saffron in the international market is about 70%. Most of the Iranian saffron is exported in bulk and dealers in Spain and USA manage the packaging, marketing and distribution therefore, most of the added value is generated and kept outside Iran. In Iran there are about 120 saffron processing and packaging enterprises of which, about 70 are formal and 50 are informal. Most of these enterprises only work in the domestic market and very few are exporters. Furthermore, most of the exporting enterprises use very basic packaging, once at destination the product is repacked accordingly to the final customer requirement. The farming component of the value chain has been largely disregarded in recent years; the productivity is very low in comparison with other production countries, about 3.5kg/Ha. In this regard, gender is a key development issue.
